entries.text: Build a small dependency-free Node.js 24 CLI called wordfreq in this repo: it prints the N most frequent words across the given text files (flags: -n <count>, --ignore-case, --min-length <k>). Work in small steps and commit after each with a conventional commit message, using plain git commit so its output is printed: 1) scaffold package.json, bin/wordfreq.js and a README; 2) implement counting with node:test tests in test/; 3) run the tests, fix whatever fails, and add an edge-case test for punctuation and unicode words; 4) add a --json output flag with a test. Run the tests before each commit. Stay inside this directory. Keep it simple.
I’ll build this in four small steps, run the tests before each commit, and use plain `git commit`.

files.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,15 @@
+# wordfreq
+
+A dependency-free Node.js 24 CLI that prints the most frequent words across text files.
+
+```sh
+node bin/wordfreq.js -n 10 --ignore-case --min-length 3 first.txt second.txt
+```
+
+Options:
+
+- `-n <count>`: maximum number of words to print. Default: 10.
+- `--ignore-case`: convert words to lowercase before counting.
+- `--min-length <k>`: minimum word length. Default: 1.
+
+Run tests with `npm test`.

Work in small steps and commit after each with a conventional commit message, using plain git commit so its output is printed: 1) scaffold package.json, bin/wordfreq.js and a README; 2) implement counting with node:test tests in test/; 3) run the tests, fix whatever fails, and add an edge-case test for punctuation and unicode words; 4) add a --json output flag with a test. Word counting and the Unicode edge-case test pass. No fixes were needed. I’ll now add `--json` with a test that checks the output.

@@ -13,2 +13,3 @@
 - `--min-length <k>`: minimum word length. Default: 1.
+- `--json`: print an array of objects with `word` and `count` fields.
 
@@ -19,3 +20,4 @@
 Length counts Unicode code points. Output is `word<TAB>count`, one word per
-line. Results sort by count, then by word in code point order for ties.
+line. Results sort by count, then by word in JavaScript string order for ties.
 Use `--` before file names that start with `-`. A count of zero prints nothing.
+With `--json`, empty results print `[]`.
